evaluations.label: A
errors: "the IS1001c remote control": no product name or code is mentioned anywhere in the transcript.

"The remote will include backlit buttons that activate upon movement" stated as a decided feature; in the transcript motion activation was questioned (needs another sensor, "too expensive") and the PM said "we will discuss that after"; it was never decided.
"an arched internal structure for component mounting": the transcript says "something odd shaped, with a spongy cover"; "arched" is invented.
"Action Items: (none)" even though the PM asked the Industrial Designer and UI Designer to work together on the prototype and listed next tasks (final look and feel, UI design, evaluation).
strengths: Correctly captures the 50x wheel cost, the 12 euro ceiling, the decision to keep the wheel, the banana shape, yellow colour, spongy material and company colour scheme.
Unresolved Questions section correctly flags the voice recognition chip as open and the battery concern on lighting.
Outline follows the meeting flow and recaps the previous decisions accurately (plastic cover, lighting, no LCD/voice).
weaknesses: Action items left empty while the outline itself mentions the collaboration instruction; a reader would miss who does what.
Presents a contested lighting mechanism as settled.
Invented details (product code, arched structure) undermine trust.
Does not mention further instructions coming by email, the pear alternative, or that the UI designer suggested the wheel push-down.

evaluations.label: B
errors: "It had a channel wheel, preview button": the transcript says "previous channel button", not a preview button.
"The wheel could be pressed down to recall a channel": the transcript says the push-down could be used "for the record if we want"; "recall a channel" is an interpretation not supported by the words.

"The group did not document a detailed resolution" on left/right handed use: the PM did state it is okay for both righty and lefty and that lighted buttons identify the right side, and the UI designer accepted with "Okay. Maybe. Yeah."; a tentative resolution was reached.
strengths: Accurate on the key numbers (50x, up to 12 euros), the ranking fancy > innovative > easy to use, and the final concept (yellow banana, wheel on top, buttons on side, spongy cover over inner structure, standard battery, chip-on-print).
Correctly notes that no decision was made on voice features and that the battery concern on continuous lighting was raised.
Next work and who does it (ID and UID together on the prototype; final look and feel, UI design, check against requirements; instructions by email) is stated correctly.
Timestamps let a reader go back to the recording.
weaknesses: Action items section is empty; the next-work items are buried as sub-bullets.
Nested bullet structure is fragmented and repeats the wheel decision three times.
Omits the lighted-buttons orientation point and the rejected ice/blue LED idea; the "not documented" phrasing on handedness undersells what was agreed.

evaluations.label: C
errors: "Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested": the PM said "something odd shaped, with a spongy cover"; heart-shaped is invented.

Action item "Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity" and "Assess cost implications of wheel sensor" for the Industrial Designer: the wheel was decided in this meeting ("we can keep the wheel ... even if the cost is a bit higher"); no follow-up on wheel cost was assigned.

"Arrange prototype development and user evaluation (20:26)" and "Coordinate final look and feel and UI collaboration (20:26)": these were said around 22:50, and the timestamps attached to several actions do not match where they were said.
"UI Designer (UL Hazred)": the name given in the transcript is "Abdul al-Hasred".
"Fancy look prioritized over function": the marketing expert ranked fancy look and feel first, technological innovation second, ease of use third; the notes drop the innovation ranking in that line.
strengths: Captures the 50x cost, 12 euro budget, plastic cover objections (breaks, harder to press, keep digits separate), symmetry concern and lighted buttons to identify the side.
Names the ID and UID collaboration on the prototype and the evaluation step.
weaknesses: Entirely omits the voice recognition chip email from the manufacturing division, the battery concern on lighting, the standard battery and chip-on-print decisions, and the no LCD/no voice prior decision.
Never clearly states that the wheel was kept or that the plastic cover was dropped; outcomes are presented as debates.
Action items are padded with invented or generic tasks and several wrong timestamps, so a reader cannot trust the list.
Too terse for someone who missed the meeting to understand why decisions were made.

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Construction: hard internal structure with spongy outer cover": the transcript says "odd shaped, with a spongy cover"; "hard" is an interpretation, though consistent with the UI designer's concern about buttons moving.
"Alternative: recess or offset channel buttons slightly": the UI designer said to put the channel numbers "somewhere a bit out of the way" and "separate a bit"; "recess" is not in the transcript.

"Industrial designer to produce final banana-form design" and "UI designer to finalize layout": the PM listed the tasks and asked the two to work together, but did not assign the look-and-feel task specifically to the ID or the UI task specifically to the UID.

"Backlit buttons confirmed": lighting was a prior decision referenced again by the PM, but this meeting did not explicitly re-confirm it; the activation mechanism and battery cost were left open, which the notes do say.
strengths: Cleanly separates the previous-meeting recap from this meeting's component decisions, so a reader knows what is new.

Correct on the numbers (50x, under 12 euros), standard battery, chip-on-print, wheel kept for innovation and ease of use, Paris/Milan trend, priority ranking, banana shape with yellow colour, wheel on top and buttons on side, left/right handedness resolution with lighted buttons.
Voice recognition update is accurate and correctly marked as deferred rather than decided.
Next Steps list the four tasks the PM named and the collaboration instruction, with a short reason for each.
weaknesses: Does not say that the voice decision was never actually revisited by the end of the meeting, nor that further instructions will come by email.
Omits the pear alternative, the rejected ice/blue LED idea, the wheel push-down idea, and the ID's point that the case design also costs money.
Role assignments in Next Steps go slightly beyond what the PM said.

rationale: D is the most useful and the most faithful on decisions: it separates the recap from new decisions, gets every number and the final concept right, marks voice as deferred, and gives clear next steps with the collaboration instruction; its only slips are small interpretations (hard structure, recess, role split). B is nearly as accurate and complete, with correct open issues and next work, but has a wrong word (preview vs previous channel button), an unsupported reading of the wheel push-down, an empty action items section and a fragmented structure. A reads well and flags the right open questions but invents a product code and an arched structure, states motion-activated lighting as decided, and lists no action items. C is the weakest: it omits the voice recognition chip and the battery concern entirely, invents a heart-shaped core, pads the action items with tasks nobody assigned and mislabels their timestamps, and never states the wheel and cover outcomes as decisions.
